statement: You are given two words, beginWord and endWord, and a dictionary wordList, written as one comma-separated string.
A transformation sequence starts at beginWord and ends at endWord. Each step changes exactly one letter, and every word after beginWord, including endWord, must appear in wordList.
Return every transformation sequence of the shortest possible length, each as its list of words. The sequences can be listed in any order. If no sequence exists, return an empty list.

examples.output: hit -> hot -> dot -> dog -> cog; hit -> hot -> lot -> log -> cog
examples.explanation: The shortest sequences have 5 words, and there are exactly two of them: one passes through dot and dog, the other through lot and log.

examples.output: hot -> hog -> dog; hot -> dot -> dog
examples.explanation: From hot, changing the last letter gives hog and changing the first letter gives dot, and each of those is one letter from dog. So there are two shortest sequences of 3 words.
cog is not in the list, so no sequence can end there and there are no ladders.

constraints: every word in wordList has the same length as beginWord
all words consist of lowercase English letters
the words in wordList are distinct
